clue.text: A maxim spoken by many

annotationWithheld.why: A maxim spoken by many (5) for MORAL: 'A maxim' defines it, but no reading of 'spoken by many' gives the letters MORAL by sound or otherwise

clue.text: It can make one act straightaway

indicators.note: the letters of 'one act' can be made into something else, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre note: something that can turn one act into instant action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' signals rearranging ONEACT into the two-word answer; 'It' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something immediately means doing it without delay, the sense of straightaway.

clue.text: One running out of clothes

parts.note: reads like someone whose wardrobe is running low, but means a person who runs naked in public

explanation.surface: Someone whose supply of clothing is running low.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dashes naked through a public event, such as a sports match, is literally running without garments.

clue.text: Legendary bird soaring, so it is written, over a Mediterranean isle

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the bird's name climbs upward, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend
sic is the Latin word used to say a quotation is written exactly so

explanation.surface: A mythical bird flying high, as the record says, over an island in the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'soaring' means the bird's name reads upwards; 'over' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean Sea, birthplace of Napoleon.

clue.text: Sikes's pet sweetmeat

definitions.meaning: Bill Sikes, the villain of Dickens's Oliver Twist, owns a dog of this name
also a hard, round, striped peppermint sweet, a British confection

explanation.surface: A Dickens villain's dog doubling as a sugary treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes's dog in Oliver Twist bears this name, and it is also the name of a round boiled mint sweet sold in Britain.

clue.text: Abnormal tides wear the river bank

indicators.note: abnormal means out of the usual order, so the letters of 'tides wear' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unusual tides eroding the bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverside or bank is the strip of land at the edge of a body of water.

clue.text: Pays bill, say, for furniture

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase for 'pays bill' is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: foots means pays (as in foots the bill), and a toll is a bill or charge, giving 'foots toll'

explanation.surface: Someone settling an invoice in exchange for a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns 'foots toll' (pays a charge) into a near-identical spoken phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool for resting the feet is an item of household furnishing.

clue.text: Country river — a Russian river

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps
the Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A geography lesson listing rivers, one of them Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the adjective, as in country life; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective describes the countryside, as opposed to the town.

clue.text: A lifetime of bridge

definitions.meaning: a life ... is the length of time someone lives
as a verb, to bridge a gap is to stretch across it, as an arch does

explanation.surface: A whole life spent playing the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the duration of a life and the distance an arch stretches across, or to stretch over.

clue.text: Artists in loco parentis

indicators.note: loco is slang for crazy, so the letters of 'parentis' go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Artists acting as guardians in place of parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like part of the Latin phrase but is the anagram signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People who paint pictures are artists working in oils or watercolour.

clue.text: The favourite's all in — made to carry a big weight

definitions.text: made to carry a big weight

indicators.note: in tells us the word 'all' goes inside the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, such as the teacher's pet; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A racing tip: the favourite has gone all in on a heavy handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The favourite's all in' reads as betting talk about the race favourite; the 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable wooden platform is built for forklifts to lift heavy loads of goods.

clue.text: Magistrate's bill

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a magistrate or judge

explanation.surface: The bill, or account, presented by a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang names a magistrate after a bird's hooked mouthpart, which is also called a bill.

clue.text: Study poetic usage in everyday speech

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
verse is writing in metre, the form of poetry

explanation.surface: Examining how poetic language crops up in ordinary talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means conversation, ordinary talk between people.

clue.text: Became comfortably established in seat on row

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back
a din is a loud noise, a racket or row

explanation.surface: Getting comfortable in a seat placed on a row in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; a settle is a high-backed bench, and row here rhymes with cow (a noisy quarrel).
explanation.definitionFit: To have grown used to a new home or job is to feel at ease and established in it.

clue.text: Diving attempts at goal

parts.note: reads as a swimmer's dives, but describes a footballer flinging himself to strike the ball with his head

explanation.surface: A diver's attempts to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, shots or passes struck with the head, sometimes with a full-length dive, are attempts to score.

clue.text: Certain people cannot be so described

definitions.text: Certain people cannot be so described

parts.words: Certain people cannot be so described
parts.note: certain here means sure of themselves, and someone sure is by definition not uncertain

explanation.surface: A remark that a particular group of people can't be described in a given way.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is sure of something is the opposite of uncertain or unsure.

clue.text: Pins one's faith on hinges

definitions.meaning: to rely on or trust in someone
to turn on or be decided by something, as in 'it all hinges on the weather'

explanation.surface: Someone trusting in door hinges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the two definitions and also completes the phrases 'relies on' and 'hinges on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both relying or trusting, and being contingent or conditional on something.

clue.text: Balanced, prepared diet that rounds off the day

parts.note: even means balanced or level

indicators.note: a prepared dish has been made up, so the letters of 'diet' are reworked

explanation.surface: A balanced, ready-made diet to finish the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' looks like food to go with the balanced meal, but its letters are only shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the time at the close of the daylight hours.

clue.text: One in dispute about a debt may hesitate

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters of 'a debt' are moved around

parts.note: er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: A debtor arguing about money owed may pause before answering.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone owing money; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues a case in a formal discussion takes part in a dispute.

clue.text: Try hard to get free labour

definitions.meaning: to wriggle and fight against restraint

explanation.surface: Making every effort to obtain unpaid work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers fighting to escape a hold, and hard toil or effort generally.

clue.text: One effect of gravity on a monkey is to yawn

indicators.note: in a down clue, one letter on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity in physics
an ape is a tailless monkey-like primate, loosely called a monkey

explanation.surface: A physics question: what happens to a monkey under gravity's pull?
explanation.walkthrough: 'One effect of' and 'is to' are links; G sits on top of APE.
explanation.definitionFit: To open the mouth wide, as when tired or astonished, is a kind of yawning.

clue.text: There's need for variety in a garden

indicators.note: variety means change, so the letters of 'need' are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A gardener's remark about planting a range of species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link; the definition is the biblical garden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve lived in the paradise garden of that name.

clue.text: In time a deserter will make mistakes

indicators.note: In at the start tells us the deserter goes inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Sooner or later a deserting soldier will slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are said to desert a sinking ship, hence the convention; 'a' and 'will make' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors found after a book is published, plural of erratum.

clue.text: Permit for chap to go on the base

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that goes on another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Al is a man's short name, standing for any chap
low means base, mean or contemptible

explanation.surface: A permit for a man to enter the military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'base' in the surface looks like a military camp but means low in character.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to give them permission.

clue.text: Sensible car-drivers do keep quiet

definitions.meaning: careful drivers fasten their seat belts

explanation.surface: Careful motorists stay silent at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fastening a seat belt, and is also a rude British command to stop talking.

clue.text: Last, despite great efforts

definitions.meaning: coming behind everyone else, at the very end

explanation.surface: Finishing in last place in spite of trying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean coming behind every other, and also nevertheless or in spite of what went before.

clue.text: Attractive type, secure in high position

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten or secure it
up means raised or aloft

explanation.surface: A good-looking person fastened in place up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamorous person whose poster is put on a wall is an object of admiration.

clue.text: Dramatic performance in translation

definitions.meaning: an interpretation of a role or piece on stage

explanation.surface: A stage performance in a translated version.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an artist's interpretation of a work and a version in another language.
